sampling.generator: Mulberry32; one continuous stream; descending Fisher-Yates on lexicographically sorted IDs; mc then pre then other
sampling.algorithm: Mulberry32: t = state += 0x6D2B79F5; t = imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1); t ^= t + imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61); return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296. For each sorted pool, descending Fisher–Yates uses floor(random() * (i+1)); take the first n. One continuous stream, mc then pre then other.

modelCardCriteria.MC.Q03: The card names the developer’s framework (Responsible Scaling Policy, Preparedness Framework, Frontier Safety Framework, Risk Management Framework, Frontier AI Framework, Advanced AI Scaling Framework, Frontier Governance Framework, or a successor). Stated if it names the framework and identifies the edition (version number, date or a link to a dated edition); partly if it names the framework without an edition. Not applicable if the card predates every framework edition of its developer.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q04: A hyperlink, address or bibliographic reference to the framework document in the card. Partly if it refers to the framework as a document without an address or reference. Not applicable if Q03 is not applicable.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q05: A sentence stating the outcome for the model in the framework’s own categories (for example, a safety level applied, a capability threshold reached or not reached, a risk category assigned), quoted. Partly if the card says a determination was made without stating its outcome, or states an outcome for some tracked domains only. Not applicable if Q03 is not applicable.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q07: The card reports that evaluations in this domain were run and states their outcome category or threshold language (policy level only). Partly if evaluations are reported without any outcome or conclusion for the domain. Radiological and nuclear evaluations are noted where reported together.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q08: The card reports that evaluations of offensive cyber capability were run and states their outcome category or threshold language (policy level only). Partly if evaluations are reported without any outcome or conclusion.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q10: The card reports that evaluations of persuasive or manipulative capability were run and states their outcome category or conclusion. Partly if evaluations are reported without an outcome. Not found includes a card that states the domain was removed from evaluation; the note says so.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q11: The card reports evaluations of the model’s own propensity or capability for deception, scheming, reward hacking, sabotage or undermining oversight, with a stated conclusion. Partly if evaluations are reported without a conclusion. Content-safety refusal tests do not meet it.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q14: A named government body (for example, the US AI Safety Institute or Center for AI Standards and Innovation, or the UK AI Safety or Security Institute) stated to have tested, evaluated or received access to the model, quoted. Partly if government testing is mentioned without naming the body.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q15: A passage stating that a decision to release, deploy or launch was made (decided, chose, deemed acceptable for deployment, determined that safeguards suffice for launch), quoted. Stated if the decision is described and its maker is identifiable: a named person, office or committee, or the developer in its own voice (“we”), which counts as the company as such. Partly if a release is stated as following from an assessment without a decision being described (“we therefore release”), if a decision is described without any maker, or if a maker is named only for a capability or safeguards determination and not for the release.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q01: A date printed on the card or its own page (publication, issue or revision date), quoted with its kind. Revision dates are listed separately. Partly if the card carries only a month or year, or only a revision date. The release date of the model is Q02.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q02: A passage of the card giving the model’s release, launch or availability date, or the release form (API, consumer product, open weights, limited preview), quoted. Stated if a date or a dated event is given; partly if only the form of release, or only a relative timing (for example, “at launch”), is given.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q06: A passage naming safeguards, protections or a safeguard standard applied because of, or in line with, the determination or threshold in Q05 (for example, a deployment or security standard named in the framework). Partly if safeguards are stated without being tied to a determination or threshold. A stated safeguard is the developer’s account, not evidence that it works.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q09: The card reports that evaluations in any of these domains were run and states their outcome category or threshold language (policy level only). Partly if evaluations are reported without any outcome or conclusion. Agentic task benchmarks reported only as product capability do not meet it.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q13: At least one external organisation (other than a government body, which is Q14) named as having tested or evaluated the model, quoted. Partly if external testers are described but not named.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q12: A passage reporting adversarial testing described as red-teaming (internal, external or both), quoted with its scope (domains, number or kind of testers, or period) where given. Partly if red-teaming is mentioned without any scope.
modelCardCriteria.MC.Q16: A passage stating a limitation, gap or uncertainty of the evaluations reported in the card (for example, that results may underestimate capability, that elicitation was incomplete, or that a threshold could not be ruled out with confidence), quoted. Limitations of the model as a product (for example, hallucination) do not meet it.
